correctness.rationale: The normalization in Ma's order-three defect was checked against Theorem 2.3 and independently by exact polynomial interpolation. With H(t)=(t+1)(t+2)(t+3), D(t)=H(t+3), R=diag(1−H/D), one has M* = BM and S=M*(I−B*B)M. The finite-support right inverse is (I−T)^3 diag(H)/6 for the unilateral shift T; multiplication on basis vectors follows by cancelling the generating series (1−z)^−3 and (1−z)^3, giving dense range. On −1<α<0 the signed weights have signs (−,+,−). Since D−H=9t²+63t+114≥60 for t≥−1, the v₂ weighted square sum is at most (1/60)Σ_{n≥0}[(n+3)(n+4)(n+5)]^−1=1/1440. Multiplication by |λ₂|≤20 and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz absorb that direction into R/72. The form is nonnegative on v₀⊥, so its pullback has negative index at most one (the preimage of v₀⊥ has codimension at most one). For 1 on 0..N and zero elsewhere, the diagonal is 9 log N+O(1), the v₀ pairing is log N+O(1), and the other pairings stay bounded; the quadratic form is 9α(log N)²+O(log N) and eventually negative for each fixed α<0. Density transfers a strict witness to S. R tends to zero and the correction has finite rank, giving compactness and exactly one negative eigenvalue with multiplicity one. Ma Theorem 1.1 supplies nonnegativity for α≥0, including zero. No finite spectral truncation was used.
